migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Ecosystem findings/citations were centrally re-adjudicated under the current runner-owned fixed rubric. Legacy language-local scores were not copied.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.candidate_universe: Predeclared sampling cells for this metric: (1) official project-declared community index page (ziglang.org/community), (2) the largest real-time chat community linked from that page (official Discord invite), (3) the officially endorsed forum that explicitly replaced the language's Reddit presence (Ziggit, a Discourse instance), (4) dedicated Q&A tag on Stack Overflow / the language's own Wikipedia-adjacent third-party coverage, (5) commercially/openly published books indexed by major publishers (O'Reilly/Packt, Manning) and by community open-access channels (GitHub Pages books), (6) third-party tag-based content aggregator (dev.to Zig tag). All six are the same class of source type used for every other assigned language in this ecosystem metric family: official docs/community page, largest chat platform, dedicated Q&A/forum, published books, third-party content aggregator. Retrieval route: web_search snapshot on 2026-09-22 (today's date per task packet), single retrieval pass per source, no re-querying after initial capture to avoid retrieval-order bias.

component_findings.current_knowledge: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--zig): The official ziglang.org community page lists a wide but fragmented array of channels: regional mailing lists, a Chinese-language forum, a Russian-language community, a 'ZigQuestions' resource, a dedicated Discord for a community show, and the Ziggit forum -- showing breadth but also dispersion of public knowledge across many small channels rather than one authoritative hub.
component_findings.events_groups: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--zig): Zig has a genuinely active, multi-channel public-knowledge ecosystem (official docs, a dedicated Discourse Q&A forum, a large Discord, several 2024-2025 published books, and recurring third-party blog/dev.to coverage), which places it above a niche/abandoned-language floor. However, its durable, crawlable, search-indexed knowledge base (Stack Overflow-style canonical Q&A) is comparatively thin, its primary community forum has suffered documented discontinuity (Reddit closure/hostile-takeover), and the language's pre-1.0 status limits accumulated historical knowledge volume relative to mature ecosystems. This nets a middling-to-moderate normalized score rather than a high or low extreme.
component_findings.international_breadth: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--zig): The official ziglang.org community page lists a wide but fragmented array of channels: regional mailing lists, a Chinese-language forum, a Russian-language community, a 'ZigQuestions' resource, a dedicated Discord for a community show, and the Ziggit forum -- showing breadth but also dispersion of public knowledge across many small channels rather than one authoritative hub.
component_findings.learning_materials: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--zig): At least three distinct dedicated Zig books exist as of the snapshot: Packt/O'Reilly's 'Learning Zig' by Alex Rios (November 2025, 502 pages, intermediate-to-advanced), Manning's 'Systems Programming with Zig' by Garrison Hinson-Hasty, and the independently published open-access 'Introduction to Zig: a project-based book' by Pedro Duarte Faria (first released October 2024, updated through Zig 0.16.0), showing a real but still-small and recent publishing footprint.
component_findings.qa_discussion: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--zig): A Hacker News discussion thread specifically about the Zig Discord raises the concern that answering questions primarily in Discord is a structural step backward from Stack-Overflow-style durable, searchable, canonical answers, since chat platforms don't preserve a crowdsourced, findable answer for future askers the way Stack Overflow does.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.limitations: Discord member counts, subreddit history, and dev.to tag activity are used only as declared corroborating evidence points within this single metric, not as a standalone score for the whole evaluation, per the ecosystem methodology's restriction on raw popularity indicators. Member/subscriber counts do not measure answer quality, duplicate/stale content, or search-engine discoverability, and Discord message volume is not publicly countable via this retrieval route, so channel-size figures are reported as one input among several qualitative structural findings (forum continuity, book count, doc format) rather than as the sole basis for the score.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Inspect the same knowledge channels for every language and use current, publicly accessible evidence rather than raw search-result counts alone.
